extraction.name: VQAonline
extraction.description: A visual question answering dataset sourced from online question answering communities in which all contents originate from an authentic use case. It includes authentic context, answers validated as acceptable by the question asker, and user-chosen topics across 105 diverse topics.
extraction.creator: Chongyan Chen, Mengchen Liu, Noel Codella, Yunsheng Li, Lu Yuan, and Danna Gurari
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was created by scraping publicly available Stack Exchange data and collecting examples that contained a natural language question, natural language context, an image, and at least one answer; only examples with an accepted answer were kept, followed by filtering out low-quality VQAs.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Public Stack Exchange archive data consisting of user-provided post titles as questions, body text as context, image URL links, answers, and accepted-answer markings from 105 topical sites.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For dataset labels, answers were provided publicly by Stack Exchange users, and the question asker could mark one answer as the "accepted answer"; the dataset kept only examples with an accepted answer. For expert evaluation, ten domain experts were hired, given a one-on-one training session, and used a web-based annotation interface with instructions; time spent per question was monitored as a quality-control proxy.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Stack Exchange for accepted-answer labeling; a custom web-based annotation tool for expert evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Quality-related analysis included reliance on Stack Exchange moderation/reputation mechanisms for answer quality, monitoring expert annotation time as a QC proxy, and reporting Spearman correlation between evaluation metrics and human judgments.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: At least one answer per item in the source data; one accepted answer retained for dataset examples. For expert evaluation, one domain expert represented each selected topic.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Stack Exchange users; for expert evaluation, annotators were domain experts located in the United States and selected to ensure English proficiency.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Potential benchmark bias exists because many evaluated models may have been trained on Stack Exchange data and thus could have seen VQAonline examples; additionally, one evaluation metric (CLIP-S) may reflect biases from its pretraining data.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The paper discusses limitations of prior VQA datasets rather than explicit limitations of VQAonline itself. It notes that existing datasets are artificially constructed, generalize poorly to authentic use cases due to domain shifts, often lack diversity, and that VizWiz-VQA is limited to one population and uses answers collected years later rather than validated by the original askers. It also notes reproducibility concerns for GPT-4V evaluation and deficiencies in standard short-answer VQA metrics for this dataset’s long answers.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is expected to support improvements in real-world VQA applications, including community question answering platforms, learning assistance tools for children, virtual assistants, visual dialog/query, and visual search/browsing. It is also intended to facilitate research on hallucination issues in authentic use cases.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for benchmarking and improving VQA models on authentic use cases, especially long-form answer generation and evaluation. It is publicly shared to encourage community-wide progress and can support future work on evaluation metrics and hallucination analysis.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset will be publicly released/shared, but no explicit maintenance schedule, versioning policy, maintainers, or deprecation policy is provided.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Filtered the scraped Stack Exchange data by keeping examples with question, context, image, and at least one answer; retaining only examples with an accepted answer; removing low-quality posts with scores of 0 or less for either the question or answer; removing questions with multiple images; removing visual questions with visual answers; removing examples whose images could not be downloaded; and converting all images to PNG format for consistency.

name.evidence: We address these limitations by introducing a new dataset called VQAonline.

description.evidence: Sourced from online question answering communities, it is the the first VQA dataset with all contents originating from an authentic use case... it contains: (1) authentic context that clarifies the question, (2) an answer the individual asking the question validated as acceptable, (3) answers that are considerably longer... and (4) user-chosen topics for each visual question from 105 diverse topics.
